spots.name: Birmingham Museum and Art Gallery

hours.note: Closed Fri, Sat, Sun

spots.summary: Birmingham Museum and Art Gallery (BM&AG) is a museum and art gallery in Birmingham, England. It has a collection of international importance covering fine art, ceramics, metalwork, jewellery, natural history, archaeology, ethnography, local history and industrial history.

names.es: Museo y Galería de Arte de Birmingham
names.it: Museo e galleria d'arte di Birmingham
names.zh: 伯明翰博物館和美術館

spots.name: St Philip's Cathedral
spots.summary: The Cathedral Church of Saint Philip, also called the Birmingham Cathedral, is a Church of England cathedral and the seat of the Bishop of Birmingham. Built as a parish church in the Baroque style by Thomas Archer, it was consecrated in 1715.

names.es: Catedral de San Felipe de Birmingham

spots.name: Library of Birmingham

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: The Library of Birmingham is a public library in Birmingham, England. It is situated on the west side of the city centre at Centenary Square, beside the Birmingham Rep and Baskerville House. Upon opening on 3 September 2013, it replaced Birmingham Central Library.

names.ja: バーミンガム公共図書館

spots.name: Victoria Square
spots.summary: Victoria Square is a pedestrianised public square in Birmingham, England. It is home to both the Town Hall and the Council House, and directly adjacent to Chamberlain Square. It is named in honour of Queen Victoria.

spots.name: Birmingham Moor Street railway station
spots.summary: Birmingham Moor Street, also known as Moor Street station, is one of three main railway stations in the city centre of Birmingham, in the West Midlands, England; the other two are New Street and Snow Hill.

names.ja: バーミンガム・ムーアストリート駅

spots.name: Birmingham Town Hall
spots.summary: Birmingham Town Hall is a concert hall and venue for popular assemblies opened in 1834 and situated in Victoria Square, Birmingham, England. It is a Grade I listed building.

spots.name: Joseph Chamberlain Memorial Clock Tower

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Joseph Chamberlain Memorial Clock Tower, or colloquially Old Joe, is a clock tower and campanile located in Chancellor's court at the University of Birmingham, in the suburb of Edgbaston. It is the tallest clock tower in the UK, although its actual height is the subject of some confusion.

names.ja: チェンバレン記念時計塔

spots.name: St Martin in the Bull Ring
spots.summary: St Martin in the Bull Ring is a Church of England parish church in the city of Birmingham, West Midlands, England. It is the original parish church of Birmingham and stands between the Bull Ring Shopping Centre and the markets.
spots.wikipediaTitle: St Martin in the Bull Ring

names.ja: セント・マーティン教会

spots.name: Council House, Birmingham
spots.summary: Birmingham City Council House in Birmingham, England, is the home of Birmingham City Council, and thus the seat of local government for the city.

spots.name: Chamberlain Square
spots.summary: Chamberlain Square or Chamberlain Place is a public square in central Birmingham, England, named after statesman and notable mayor of Birmingham, Joseph Chamberlain.

spots.name: Birmingham Central Library

hours.note: Closed Sun; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Birmingham Central Library was the main public library in Birmingham, England, from 1974 until 2013, replacing a library opened in 1865 and rebuilt in 1882. For a time the largest non-national library in Europe, it closed on 29 June 2013 and was replaced by the Library of Birmingham.

names.ja: バーミンガム中央図書館

spots.name: St Chad's Cathedral

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Metropolitan Cathedral Church and Basilica of Saint Chad is a Catholic cathedral in Birmingham, England. It is the mother church of the Archdiocese of Birmingham and is dedicated to Saint Chad of Mercia.

spots.name: Alpha Tower

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Alpha Tower is a Grade II listed office skyscraper in Birmingham, England.

spots.name: Centenary Square
spots.summary: Centenary Square is a public square on the north side of Broad Street in Birmingham, England, named in 1989 to commemorate the centenary of Birmingham achieving city status.

spots.name: Aston Hall

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Aston Hall is a Grade I listed Jacobean house in Aston, Birmingham, England, designed by John Thorpe and built between 1618 and 1635. It is a leading example of the Jacobean prodigy house.

spots.name: Hall of Memory, Birmingham

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: The Hall of Memory is a war memorial in Centenary Square, Birmingham, England, designed by S. N. Cooke and W. N. Twist. Erected 1922–25 by John Barnsley and Son, it commemorates the 12,320 Birmingham citizens who died in World War I.

spots.name: Birmingham Walk of Stars
spots.summary: The Birmingham Walk of Stars is a walk of fame-style installation on the pedestrian pavement of Broad Street in Birmingham, England, which honours notable people from the Birmingham area or with significant connections with it. The scheme is organised and funded by the Broad Street Business Improvement District.

spots.name: Thinktank

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue

spots.summary: Thinktank, Birmingham is a science museum in Birmingham, England. Opened in 2001, it is part of Birmingham Museums Trust and is located within the Millennium Point complex on Curzon Street, Digbeth.

names.ja: バーミンガム・サイエンス・ミュージアム
names.zh: 智库伯明翰科学博物馆

spots.name: The Octagon

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Octagon is a 155 m (509 ft) tall, 49-storey residential skyscraper in Birmingham, England. The building is part of the Paradise redevelopment scheme in the city centre and is designed by Glenn Howells Architects.

spots.name: A Real Birmingham Family
spots.summary: A Real Birmingham Family is a public artwork and sculpture by Gillian Wearing, cast in bronze, and erected in Centenary Square, outside the Library of Birmingham, England, on 30 October 2014.

spots.name: Boulton, Watt and Murdoch
spots.summary: Boulton, Watt and Murdoch is a gilded bronze statue depicting Matthew Boulton, James Watt, and William Murdoch by William Bloye, assisted by Raymond Forbes Kings.

names.ja: ボールトン、ワットそしてマードック

spots.name: Iron:Man
spots.summary: Iron:Man is a statue by Antony Gormley, in Victoria Square, Birmingham, England. The statue is 6 metres (20 ft) tall, including the feet which are buried beneath the pavement, and weighs 6 metric tons. The statue leans 7.5° backwards and 5° to its left.

spots.name: Symphony Hall
spots.summary: Symphony Hall is a 2,262-seat concert venue in Birmingham, England. It was officially opened by Queen Elizabeth II on 12 June 1991, although it had been in use since 15 April 1991. It is home to the City of Birmingham Symphony Orchestra and hosts around 270 events a year. It was completed at a cost of £30 million.

names.ja: シンフォニー・ホール (バーミンガム)

spots.name: Broad Street
spots.summary: Broad Street is a major thoroughfare and popular nightspot centre in Central Birmingham, England.

spots.name: Cadbury World
spots.summary: Cadbury World is a visitor attraction in Bournville, Birmingham, England, featuring a self-guided exhibition tour, created and run by the Cadbury Company. The tour tells the history of chocolate, and of the Cadbury business.

names.ja: キャドバリーワールド

spots.name: Birmingham Back to Backs

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu

spots.summary: The Birmingham Back to Backs are the city's last surviving court of back-to-back houses. They are preserved as examples of the thousands of similar houses that were built around shared courtyards, for the rapidly increasing population of Britain's expanding industrial towns.

names.ja: バーミンガム・バック・トゥ・バックス

spots.name: St Paul's Church

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St Paul's is a Church of England church in the Georgian St Paul's Square in the Jewellery Quarter, Birmingham, England.

spots.name: Colmore Row
spots.summary: Colmore Row is a street in Birmingham City Centre in the centre of Birmingham, England, running from Victoria Square to just beyond Snow Hill station. It is traditionally the city's most prestigious business address.

spots.name: BT Tower

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The BT Tower, formerly known as the Post Office Tower and the GPO Tower, is a landmark and telecommunications tower in Birmingham, England. Until 2024 it was the tallest structure in the city, being surpassed by the topping out of both the Octagon and One Eastside that year, which now share the title.

spots.name: Birmingham Oratory

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Birmingham Oratory is a Roman Catholic religious community of the Oratory of St. Philip Neri, located in the Edgbaston area of Birmingham. The community was founded in 1849 by John Henry Newman as the first house of that congregation in England.

names.ja: バーミンガムオラトリオ会

spots.name: Barber Institute of Fine Arts

hours.note: Closed Sun

spots.summary: The Barber Institute of Fine Arts is an art gallery and concert hall in Birmingham, England. It is situated in purpose-built premises on the campus of the University of Birmingham.

names.ja: バーミンガム大学付属バーバー美術館

spots.name: Big Brum

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Big Brum is the local name for the clock tower on the Council House, Birmingham, England. Built in 1885, the clock tower is part of the first extension to the original Council House of 1879 and stands above the Museum & Art Gallery.

spots.name: National Sea Life Centre
spots.summary: The National Sea Life Centre is an aquarium with over 60 displays of freshwater and marine life in Brindleyplace, Birmingham, England.

spots.name: Galton Bridge
spots.summary: The Galton Bridge is a cast-iron bridge in Smethwick, near Birmingham, in the West Midlands of England. Opened in 1829 as a road bridge, the structure has been pedestrianised since the 1970s.

spots.name: Wheel of Birmingham
spots.summary: The Wheel of Birmingham or Birmingham Wheel was a series of transportable Ferris wheel installations at Centenary Square in Birmingham, England. These have been landmarks in central Birmingham, visible from many parts of the city.

spots.name: 10 Holloway Circus

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: 10 Holloway Circus is a 400-foot (122 m) tall mixed-use skyscraper in Birmingham city centre, England. It was originally named after the developers, Beetham Organisation, and was designed by Ian Simpson and built by Laing O'Rourke. The entire development covers an area of 7,000 square feet (650 m2).

spots.name: Castle Bromwich Hall
spots.summary: Castle Bromwich Hall is a Jacobean mansion in the Castle Bromwich area of Solihull, England. It is a Grade I listed building.

spots.name: Statue of Horatio Nelson
spots.summary: The Statue of Horatio Nelson, 1st Viscount Nelson, by Richard Westmacott stands in the Bull Ring, Birmingham, England.

spots.name: Sarehole Mill

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Sarehole Mill is a Grade II listed water mill, in an area once called Sarehole, on the River Cole in Hall Green, Birmingham, England. It is now run as a museum by the Birmingham Museums Trust. It is known for its association with J. R. R.

spots.name: Villa Park
spots.summary: Villa Park is a football stadium in Aston, Birmingham, with a seating capacity of 43,205. It has been the home of Premier League club Aston Villa since 1897.

spots.name: Soho House

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue, Thu, Fri, Sat, Sun

spots.summary: Soho House is a museum run by Birmingham Museums Trust, celebrating Matthew Boulton's life, his partnership with James Watt, his membership of the Lunar Society of Birmingham and his contribution to the Midlands Enlightenment and the Industrial Revolution.

spots.name: Birmingham Botanical Gardens
spots.summary: The Birmingham Botanical Gardens are a 15-acre (6-hectare) botanical garden situated in Edgbaston, Birmingham, England. The gardens are located 1+1⁄2 miles (2.4 km) south-west of Birmingham city centre at grid reference SP049854.

spots.name: Chamberlain Clock

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Chamberlain Clock is an Edwardian, cast-iron, clock tower in the Jewellery Quarter of Birmingham, England. It was erected in 1903 to mark Joseph Chamberlain's tour of South Africa between 26 December 1902 and 25 February 1903, after the end of the Second Boer War.

spots.name: Church of the Messiah, Birmingham

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Church of the Messiah, Birmingham was a Unitarian place of worship on Broad Street. The impressive Victorian Gothic church was constructed between 1860-1862 and straddled the Birmingham Canal. The congregation pre-dates the building, and has continued following its demolition in 1978.

spots.name: St Jude's Church, Birmingham

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: St Jude's Church, Birmingham was a parish church in the Church of England in Birmingham.

photo.author: Elliott Brown from Birmingham, United Kingdom

spots.name: Birmingham Central Mosque

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Birmingham Central Mosque, is a mosque in the Highgate area of Birmingham, England, run by the Birmingham Mosque Trust. The organization, 'Muslims in Britain’ classify the Birmingham Central Mosque as, nonsectarian. The mosque has a capacity of 6,000, including women.

spots.name: Alexandra Theatre
spots.summary: The Alexandra, commonly known as the Alex, is a theatre on Suffolk Queensway in Birmingham, England.

spots.name: Metchley Fort
spots.summary: Metchley Fort was a Roman fort in what is now Birmingham, England. It was built across four phases using a north-to-south plan.

spots.name: Birmingham Wildlife Conservation Park
spots.summary: Birmingham Wildlife Conservation Park, formerly Birmingham Nature Centre, and before that Birmingham Zoo, is a small zoo on the edge of Cannon Hill Park in Birmingham, England. It is owned and managed by Birmingham City Council.

names.ja: バーミンガム・ネイチャー・センター

spots.name: Five Ways
spots.summary: Five Ways is an area of Central Birmingham, England. It takes its name from a major road junction, now a busy roundabout to the south-west of the city centre which lies at the outward end of Broad Street, where the Birmingham Middle ring road crosses the start of the A456.

spots.name: St Paul's Square
spots.summary: St Paul's Square is a Georgian square in the Jewellery Quarter, Birmingham, England, named after the church at its centre. It is the last remaining Georgian Square in the city.

spots.name: Snowhill

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Snowhill is a mixed-use development in the Colmore business district, known historically as Snow Hill, in Central Birmingham, England. The area, between Snow Hill Queensway and Birmingham Snow Hill station, was redeveloped in 2020 by the Ballymore Group.

photo.author: Elliott Brown from Birmingham, United Kingdom

spots.name: Birmingham Proof House

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Birmingham Gun Barrel Proof House is a weapons proving establishment in Banbury Street, Birmingham, UK. The building was designed by John Horton and consists of a centre bay, emphasised by a segmental parapet, which contains trophies by William Hollins. A Jacobean-style gateway was added in 1883.

spots.name: The Old Rep
spots.summary: The Old Rep is a historic Grade II listed theatre, located on Station Street in Birmingham, England.

spots.name: Eastside City Park
spots.summary: Eastside City Park is a 6.75 acre urban park located in the Eastside district of Birmingham City Centre. Designed by architects Patel taylor with landscape architect Allain Provost, the park was opened to the public on 5 December 2012 at a cost of £11.75 million.

spots.name: Lapworth Museum of Geology
spots.summary: The Lapworth Museum of Geology is a geological museum run by the University of Birmingham and located on the university's campus in Edgbaston, south Birmingham, England. The museum is named after the geologist Charles Lapworth, its origins dating back to 1880.

names.zh: 拉普沃茲地質學博物館

spots.name: Singers Hill Synagogue

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: The Singers Hill Synagogue, officially the Birmingham Hebrew Congregation, is an Orthodox Jewish congregation and synagogue, located at 26, 26A and 26B Blucher Street, in the Birmingham city centre, in the West Midlands of England, in the United Kingdom.

spots.name: Methodist Central Hall, Birmingham
spots.summary: The Methodist Central Hall, at 196–224 Corporation Street, Birmingham, England, is a three-storey red brick and terracotta Grade II* listed building with a distinctive tower at the northern end of Corporation Street.

spots.name: Key Hill Cemetery
spots.summary: Key Hill Cemetery, originally called Birmingham General Cemetery, is a cemetery in Hockley, Birmingham, England. It opened in 1836 as a nondenominational cemetery, and is the oldest cemetery, not being in a churchyard, in Birmingham.

spots.name: The Bartons Arms
spots.summary: The Bartons Arms is a public house in the High Street in the Newtown area of Aston, Birmingham, England.

spots.name: Hudson's Coffee House
spots.summary: The former coffee house is a rare, Grade I listed, example of a wall-to-wall townhouse in the Arts & Crafts style. It was built to house offices of the Eagle Insurance Company in 1900.

spots.name: Rotunda
spots.summary: The Rotunda was devised as a 25-storey office building in a round shape, from which it derives its name. In many ways, it was a groundbreaking and daring engineering and architectural feat when it was constructed, and because of this is Grade II listed. In the 2000s it was thoroughly refurbished as a residential tower with 232 luxury apartments. Those on floors 19 and 20 are available for short te

spots.name: IKON Gallery

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Small gallery with two or three temporary modern and conceptual art installations. Excellent cafe (see below).

spots.name: Bell Edison Telephone Building
spots.summary: A signature, Grade-I-listed, building for the red-brick-and-terracota Victorian style prevalent in the late 19th century in Birmingham, which lacked natural stone and battled sooting problems due to air pollution. It is also a symbol of modernisation of Birmingham, as it was built to house the Central Telephone Exchange for the city; the logos of the Bell-Edison company are still visible within th

spots.name: The Coffin Works

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue

spots.summary: An industrial heritage museum in the Jewellery Quarter, dedicated to educating visitors about the social and industrial history and importance of the site which was in operation as a coffin furniture factory from 1894 to its closure in 1998. Ornaments made by the Newman Brothers decorated the coffins of Sir Winston Churchill, Joseph Chamberlain, and many others. Many of the historic rooms, among w

spots.name: The Old Crown
spots.summary: The Old Crown lays claim to being the oldest building in Birmingham (purportedly there since 1368, although almost all of the present timber-framed building dates from the early 16th century). Saved from demolition multiple times, it remains an operational pub, also serving food.

names.ja: ジ・オールド・クラウン

spots.name: Royal Birmingham Society of Artists

hours.note: Closed Mon; Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Independent art gallery; frequent temporary exhibitions and works for sale.

spots.name: The Queens Arms

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: A great place to watch live sport and the venue of the best quiz night in Birmingham every Thursday night. It's just £1 to enter and there's no limit on the size of the teams. A great night out for seasoned quiz-goers and first-timers alike. Homemade pizzas and a sausage selection giving a fresh choice every day, also has two for one offers every weekday. Great place for traditional ales and a Cas

spots.name: The Wellington

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: An outstanding and frequently-changing selection of well-kept real ales, lagers, ciders and perry (the current list can be viewed on-line), run by knowledgeable CAMRA members. No food served, but condiments, cutlery and crockery are available to people bringing their own (supermarkets and fast-food premsises are nearby).

spots.name: The Malt House

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Make no mistake this is a chain pub serving standard food and drinks. However, when the sun is shining it is difficult to find a nicer place to drink along Birmingham's canals as there is a plethora of outdoor seating. Visited by Bill Clinton during his Birmingham visit.

spots.name: Rectory Bar & Restaurant

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Ideal venue for both drinking and dining with a fabulous reputation for food. Quality steaks, fresh fish, set price menu and superb wine list. The bar is vibrant every weekend and is open to 1AM. It's a stylish place but friendly and attracts a great mix of people.

spots.name: Wagamama bullring

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri, Sat

spots.summary: Birmingham's restaurant of the Wagamama chain, tidy and minimal inside with a good, varied noodle menu. Specials change frequently and there are a few good vegetarian dishes. Can get busy, with a typical wait from 10-15 minutes during peak shopping times.

spots.name: Sobar

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Sun

spots.summary: Supposedly a noodle bar, as evidence by a small noodle based menu. Really this is just a pretty decent bar/nightclub. It stocks the standard beers and drinks as well as a number of rarer Asian beers. Has a number of extremely comfortable sofas.

spots.name: Bacchus

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Cheerfully ornate, gothic style cellar bar beneath The Burlington Hotel. Discretely hidden just off the bustling New Street. Bacchus is a relaxing oasis away from the buzz of the City Centre. A range of real ales is available. Over 21s only.

spots.name: The Fighting Cocks

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Very pleasant pub with a youngish crowd in the centre offering a selection of traditional pub food and more modern dishes and vast selection of beers and wine. Not cheap for pub food slow service but good quality.

spots.name: Cafe Face

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Excellent reputation for their roasted vegetables or jacket potatoes. Absolutely excellent cafes, big helpings not shy on the cheese, garlic mayonnaise and chilli sauce if you were to order them.

spots.name: The Junction

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: An odd V shaped pub as the name suggests on the junction of the High Street and Vivian Road. A really nice pub sells some real ales and good selection of lagers. Sells good pub grub as well.

spots.name: Bambu

hours.note: Closed Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Sat, Sun

spots.summary: One of the best, but also one of the most pretentious clubs in Birmingham. It's not cheap but is still the place to be seen. The dress code here is very hard to define, they want "cool".

spots.name: Java Roastery

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: An internet cafe offering a wide selection of hot drinks and cakes. Probably more genuine cafe that happens to do internet connections, than your typical scummy internet cafe.

spots.name: LEON New Street Station

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Leon serves high quality tasty food and extremely quickly when on the move. They have a great vegan selection as well. Relaxing atmosphere and wonderful decor.

spots.name: Canalside Cafe

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Fairly small cafe with a good range of organic and vegetarian foods. Excellent in the summer, as it's (unsurprisingly) right on the canalside.

spots.name: Grand Central Kitchen

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Perfect English breakfast. You can fully comprehend why there is a queue outside on a Sunday for breakfast because the food is so good.

spots.name: Edmunds Lounge Bar and Eatery

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Popular venue in the financial part of town, great food available every day. Known for quality pub food from local suppliers.

spots.name: Rock Charcoal Grill

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Halal grill serving charcoal chicken and kobedah kebab, plus curries, biryani, pizza, burgers and wraps. Eat in or take away.

spots.name: The Kitchen Garden Cafe

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Picturesque area in the middle of a busy and bustling Birmingham suburb. Quality vegetarian options and excellent service.

spots.name: Yorks Cafe

hours.note: Closed Mon

spots.summary: Modern cafe attached to the art gallery with efficient and friendly staff. Another branch is at Stephenson Street, B2 4BH.

spots.name: Whats Cooking: Rooster Chicken

hours.note: Typical hours — check the official site

spots.summary: Delicious, slightly suspect chicken in huge quantities but don't order off the board or you'll be waiting all day
